narrative_markdown:
## Overview
This afternoon update confirms that dry, warm conditions remain fully on track across Kisumu and the Nyanza Basin today, with daytime high temperatures peaking near 31°C / 88°F. No material changes have occurred to today's weather setup since the morning issuance. Focus shifts toward tonight and tomorrow, as conditions will stay calm and dry through late evening before low-level moisture begins building into Western Kenya on Sunday.

## Today's Forecast
Afternoon temperatures will max out around 31°C / 88°F before dropping to an overnight low of 18°C / 64°F. Rain probability remains near zero for the remainder of the afternoon, with only an isolated 10-20% chance of light drizzle (0.0 mm / 0.00 in) around dusk along the immediate Winam Gulf shoreline. Winds over land will maintain a southwesterly lake-breeze flow at 18 km/h (10 kt) from the SW with localized gusts reaching 35 km/h (19 kt). Peak solar UV index reaches a Very High 8.9. Air quality remains in the Moderate range (US EPA AQI 86, PM2.5 up to 48.2 μg/m³ based on CAMS model guidance, as all ground monitoring stations are currently reporting stale data).

## Extended Outlook
Near-term (Days 1–3, Sunday through Tuesday): Low-level moisture increases on Sunday (Aug 16), bringing the highest near-term likelihood of light afternoon showers (1.0 mm to 3.5 mm / 0.04 in to 0.14 in) with highs near 30°C / 86°F and lows around 20°C / 68°F. Monday (Aug 17) and Tuesday (Aug 18) will see localized shower risks (0.4 mm to 2.6 mm / 0.02 in to 0.10 in) under partly cloudy skies.
Extended (Days 4–7, Wednesday through Saturday): Convective instability expands across Western Kenya mid-to-late week, favoring more structured afternoon showers and thunderstorms on Aug 20–21 with daily precipitation totals reaching 4.2 mm / 0.17 in. High temperatures will range between 28°C / 82°F and 32°C / 90°F. Extended guidance draws on model track records at Day+3 and Day+7 where verification history is actively accumulating.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe weather, flash flooding, or significant convective hazards are expected for Kisumu or neighboring lowland counties for the remainder of today or tonight. High solar radiation (UV index 8.9) remains the primary daytime risk. Surface wind gusts along the immediate lakefront may briefly touch 35 km/h (19 kt) during peak afternoon heating.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Lake Victoria open waters will experience southwesterly winds at 18 km/h (10 kt) from the SW through dusk, with peak afternoon gusts reaching 35 km/h (19 kt) over southern channels. Overnight winds will ease and shift toward the south at 8 km/h (4 kt) from the S. Wave conditions will stay calm to light chop into Sunday morning, making overnight navigation favorable.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
The regional synoptic environment across the Nyanza Basin is anchored by an equatorial pressure ridge, maintaining mean sea-level pressure between 1013 hPa and 1015 hPa across monitoring points (Kisumu 1013.2 hPa, Busia 1013.6 hPa, Kisii 1015.5 hPa). Afternoon solar heating induced a moderate diurnal pressure dip toward 1009.6 hPa, sharpening the land-lake thermal gradient and pulling the southwesterly lake breeze onshore. Mid-level moisture remains sparse and CAPE is restricted (< 380 J/kg according to ECMWF and Best Match guidance), keeping cloud development harmless through tonight.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecaster confidence for dry conditions through tonight is high, grounded in firm agreement across GFS, ECMWF, ICON, and UKMO. Model track record evaluations at Day+0 show ECMWF and ICON leading in high-temperature precision (errors < 0.3°C), whereas GFS and UKMO display a persistent surface wind speed high bias (+15 to +20 km/h). Wind forecasts today are weighted toward ICON and ECMWF.
Ground AQI stations at Kisumu Airport, Ochieng' Avenue (Kisumu Central), and Dunga Beach have not transmitted fresh data in 9 hours (stale readings), so current air quality evaluations rely entirely on CAMS atmospheric modeling showing Moderate conditions (AQI ~86).

morning_issuance.narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Warm and mostly sunny conditions will dominate Kisumu and the broader Nyanza Basin today, with daytime highs reaching around 30°C / 86°F. Weather conditions will feel similar to yesterday, remaining dry through the morning and early afternoon before cloud cover increases slightly by dusk with a minor risk of isolated drizzle.

## Today's Forecast
Temperatures will rise from a morning low of 18°C / 64°F to an afternoon high of 30°C / 86°F. Rainfall likelihood remains low across Kisumu, with dry conditions expected for most of the day and only a minor 17-39% chance of light drizzle (0.0 mm to 0.1 mm / 0.00 in) around dusk. Daytime winds over land will start light from the northeast before shifting to a southwesterly lake breeze reaching 18 km/h (10 kt) from the SW in the late afternoon. The peak UV index will reach a Very High 8.9 near solar noon, requiring sun protection between 10:00 and 15:00 EAT. Air quality across Kisumu is in the Moderate range (US EPA AQI 86-89, PM2.5 up to 48.2 μg/m³), based on CAMS model guidance as ground monitoring sensors are currently reporting stale readings.

## Extended Outlook
Over the next 3 days (Sunday through Tuesday), a modest return of low-level moisture will gradually increase shower chances across the Nyanza Basin. Sunday (Aug 16) brings the highest near-term likelihood of light showers (1.0 mm to 3.5 mm / 0.04 in to 0.14 in) with highs near 30°C / 86°F and lows around 19°C / 66°F. Monday (Aug 17) and Tuesday (Aug 18) will feature scattered afternoon clouds and localized shower risks (1.0 mm to 8.4 mm / 0.04 in to 0.33 in). In the extended 4-to-7 day outlook (Wednesday, Aug 19 through Saturday, Aug 22), convective instability increases across Western Kenya, supporting more widespread afternoon shower and thunderstorm activity around Aug 20-21. Daytime highs will remain steady between 28°C / 82°F and 30°C / 86°F. Note that extended guidance draws on model track records at Day+3 and Day+7 where evaluation history is still accumulating.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
No severe weather, flash flooding, or widespread thunderstorm hazards are anticipated today for Kisumu or neighboring lowland counties. Localized surface wind gusts along the immediate lake shore during the afternoon wind shift could briefly reach 32 km/h (17 kt). Solar radiation hazards are elevated due to a UV index max of 8.9.

## Lake Victoria — Conditions for Boaters
Open waters of Lake Victoria will experience breezy conditions during the morning hours, with southerly to south-southeasterly winds reaching 30 km/h (16 kt) from the SSE and gusts up to 40 km/h (22 kt). Waves will be moderately choppy during early morning hours before winds veer to the southwest and ease to 16 km/h (9 kt) from the SW by late afternoon. Vessel operators and fishermen should exercise caution during early morning navigation, particularly in exposed southern channels.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
The synoptic scale over East Africa is governed by a stable equatorial pressure ridge across the Nyanza Basin, with mean sea-level pressure holding steady between 1013 hPa and 1015 hPa across regional points (Kisumu 1013.3 hPa, Busia 1013.8 hPa, Kisii 1015.4 hPa). Diurnal heating will drive a moderate pressure drop during the afternoon to ~1009 hPa, establishing a weak thermal trough over the Winam Gulf that draws a southwesterly lake breeze onshore after 13:00 EAT. Mid-level moisture remains relatively constrained today, keeping CAPE values low over Kisumu (under 350 J/kg according to ECMWF/Best Match), though localized moisture convergence at the lake-land boundary may generate isolated late-afternoon cloudiness and brief drizzle.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Forecast confidence for today's dry-to-drizzle call is high, backed by multi-model consensus (GFS, ICON, UKMO all showing 0 mm precipitation, ECMWF showing minimal 0.1 mm). Model track record analysis shows that ICON and GFS have performed strongly on daytime high temperatures (errors < 0.3°C) and pressure trends at Day+0, whereas UKMO and GFS have consistently overpredicted surface wind speeds by 15-20 km/h. Consequently, surface wind forecasts today have been weighted more towards ICON and ECMWF guidance. While all models currently have null rain trend deltas due to limited historical evaluation windows, recent verification results from yesterday confirm strong model agreement on regional precipitation boundaries.

Ground air quality readings from Kisumu Airport (AQI 61), Ochieng' Avenue, Kisumu Central (AQI 41), and Dunga Beach (AQI 78) are currently stale (3 hours old), so primary reliance is placed on CAMS atmospheric modeling showing Moderate conditions (AQI ~87).
